scope: New M1/M5 tooling source only; not a release/device certification

logic_errors.trigger: run() finally block: any exception before the save-restore step (e.g. shutil.copy2 of the log, out/watch.stop touch, watcher.wait, stop_owned raising 'owned runtime did not stop') aborts the finally block, so `shutil.rmtree(save); shutil.copytree(owner, save)` is never executed and the device is left on the control/game save instead of the owner save.
logic_errors.minimal_fix: Make the owner-save restore guaranteed, e.g. wrap the restore in its own try/finally or compute the restore last with the risky steps guarded so that a copy/kill failure cannot skip restoration.

logic_errors.trigger: In run() finally, the `if pids('wol-horizon'): raise RuntimeError('unowned runtime exists; refusing save overwrite')` check is placed BEFORE the owner save restore. If a leftover runtime exists, the raise skips restoration and the owner's save-laboratory remains replaced by the control/game data (data loss).
logic_errors.minimal_fix: Restore the owner save first (from the already-verified out/owner-save backup), verify `manifest(save)==original`, then raise on the leftover runtime; never leave the device on the control save.

suggestions.note: The candidate loop asserts candidate dims == baseline dims // 2 while the original loop asserts (w,h) == original >> (1 + clevels[id]). These only agree when clevels[id] == 1 and the baseline is exactly original >> 1; document or assert that invariant so a level value > 1 cannot silently produce a wrong but passing slice offset.

declaration() assumes the header declares `struct name { ... }` (not `typedef struct { ... } name;`) and that the struct has no nested braces; a typedef-anonymous struct or a nested enum/union would stop silently/misparse. Consider failing with a clearer message or preprocessing more robustly.

Observer binds layout to sha256 of /proc/pid/exe; when the process is binfmt/qemu-interpreted or launched from a copied binary, /proc/pid/exe may differ from the build ELF used to compile the layout, causing an exact-ELF mismatch at collect time. If so this should be a controlled failure rather than a surprise mid-run ValueError (it does not cause data loss because finally restores).

initial_review.summary: Staging code (wol_m4_stage_wave2, verify_wol_wave2) preserves accepted baseline IDs, uses conservative allowlists, and refrains from device claims; the contract tests are internally consistent and pass synthetically. The blocking defect is in wol_memory_benchmark.run(): teardown exceptions or a leftover 'wol-horizon' process skip the owner-save restore, leaving the device save replaced by the control/game save and causing data loss. The restore must be made exception-safe and performed before raising on a leftover runtime.
